gaps.title: WorldSimulation live state has no capture path at all
gaps.detail: Player position/scene, monsters (incl. wall-clock telegraph_until_ms / next_attack_ms), ground items plus the town stash, pre-instance position stash, engaged_by gate, VesselForge stream, and the world_random_state_ splitmix64 counter exist only in memory. The only serialization touching this layer is the lossy wire JSON projection. A crash, restart, or save/load boundary cannot be replayed because no canonical bytes for this layer exist.

gaps.title: Wall-clock-keyed combat/transient outcomes are unreproducible from commands alone
gaps.detail: process_combat/advance_combat take transport-supplied now_ms; monster swing windows (+1200/+1500 ms), player attack interval, boss telegraphs, respawn protection, and first-goal timestamps are wall-clock deadlines. Two byte-identical command streams through the server produce different combat timelines depending on tick-thread jitter.

gaps.title: session_rng_ stream position unrecorded
gaps.detail: dev:give/dev:drop without an explicit seed draw from the session Mulberry32 whose state is never captured; repeated identical dev requests diverge after any stream consumption elsewhere.

gaps.title: passive_tree_ accepts unversioned client payloads
gaps.detail: The skill-tree snapshot arrives raw from the client and is stored wholesale; no schema version, size bound, or validation gates this adapter input.

gaps.title: GroundItem placement ordering counter is ephemeral
gaps.detail: timestamp = ++serial_ drives newest-first menus but resets per WorldSimulation construction and is absent from every capture; ordering-sensitive UI outcomes are not reproducible across restarts.

gaps.title: File adapter unwired in production
gaps.detail: persistence::write_atomic/read are proven only by a unit test against a temp path; no production code saves or restores House bytes end-to-end, so cross-restart replay is structurally unproven.
